history.summary: IDENTITY NOTE: the CSV name 'Hanuman Temple, Yamunanagar' is generic; the most documented Hanuman shrine of the district is the Shree Panchmukhi Hanuman Mandir at Basatian Wala village on the Bilaspur-Chhachhrauli road (CSV town corrected: Bilaspur, not Yamunanagar town). Dedicated to the five-faced (Panchmukhi) form of Hanuman - the faces being Hanuman, Narasimha, Garuda, Varaha and Hayagriva. The temple trust dates its establishment to 1978. Age is disputed: Tripadvisor reviewers call it roughly 50-70 years old, while some devotees claim around 600 years and a self-manifested (svayambhu) idol - these older claims are unverified oral tradition, flagged here rather than smoothed over. It draws heavy crowds on Tuesdays and Saturdays, with Tuesday langar/bhandara and evening aarti.

name: Shree Panchmukhi Hanuman Mandir, Basatian Wala
town_description: Bilaspur is a town in Yamunanagar district, Haryana, about 30 km east of Yamunanagar city on the Bilaspur-Chhachhrauli road. It is a small agricultural market town in the Shivalik foothills region of the district.

travel.road: On the Bilaspur-Chhachhrauli road, ~4 km from Bilaspur and ~5 km from Chhachhrauli

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; Hanuman Jayanti (March-April) and the annual Maha Jagran are the main events
visitor_information.opening_hours: 5:00 AM - 12:00 PM and 4:00 PM - 9:00 PM (per the temple trust website; actual hours may vary)
